- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days) — cap forecast growth after 2-3 consecutive days of high sentiment or price surge.
- Forecast horizon 30d often lags true price movements by 1-3 days; shift forecast slightly upward for early horizon (e.g., 10d) if sentiment is bullish.
- If last 3-5 days show strong upward momentum + positive sentiment, model tends to overshoot; apply a 5-10% downward correction to avoid overbought bias.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often underestimates; add 2-5% to forecast to account for latent volatility.
- Avoid forecasting sharp downward moves unless sentiment is clearly negative and sustained; model tends to underestimate downside risk in such cases.
